claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr requires improved oxidation protection for high-temperature use in air.
Uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation and associated mechanical weakening in air at temperatures of at least 800 °C.
A silicide coating can be deposited on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by pack cementation at 1000–1100 °C under an inert atmosphere.
Several hours of pack cementation will produce a silicide coating approximately 50–100 µm thick.
The treatment will form a stable silicon-rich diffusion barrier on the alloy surface.
The silicon-rich layer will form and maintain a stable oxide scale that inhibits oxygen penetration into the HfNbTaTiZr matrix.
Oxidation of the silicide coating will yield an adherent, slow-growing oxide scale composed primarily of silica.
The silica scale will prevent rapid oxidation and protect the bulk alloy from oxygen embrittlement.
Relative to uncoated samples, coated HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit lower oxide-scale growth after five hours in air at 800–1000 °C.
The coating will reduce oxidation mass gain by at least one order of magnitude relative to uncoated HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will cause only minimal degradation of room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical properties after five hours in air.
The proposed protection is applicable up to 1000 °C for five-hour air exposures, including loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Performance during longer exposures or above 1000 °C has not been demonstrated.
A controlled test can compare identically prepared coated and uncoated HfNbTaTiZr samples using mass gain, scale thickness and composition, and post-exposure mechanical properties.
The hypothesis is falsified if coated samples show oxidation and mechanical degradation comparable to uncoated controls under identical conditions.
